chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, or from a man, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) described the cooked drink to me, how it is to be cooked until it becomes permissible, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Take a quarter of raisins, clean them, and pour twelve ratls of water over it, then soak it overnight. So when it is the days of summer and you fear that it will simmer, place it in an oven, a little full, until it does not simmer. Then remove all the water from it until morning, pour upon it water sufficient to submerge it, then boil it until its sweetness is gone.'

Then remove the last water and pour the first water over it, then measure all of it and see how much water there is, then measure a third of it and place it in the vessel in which you intend to cook it, and pour water sufficient to submerge it, and measure it with a stick, making its measure a cane or a stick, and mark it at the end of the water. Then boil the final third until the remaining water evaporates. Then boil it by the fire and do not cease boiling it until two-thirds evaporate and one-third remains.

Then take for every quarter a ratl of honey, boil it until the foam of the honey goes away and the mist of the honey goes away in the cooked drink. Then strike it with a stick with a strong strike until it mixes, and if you wish to perfume it with something from saffron or with something from ginger, do so. Then drink it, and if you wish for its staying with you to be prolonged, keep it clean.

key_terms.الْمَطْبُوخ: The cooked drink (a specific type of fermented beverage)

ai.seo_question: How to prepare a permissible fermented drink according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This detailed hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'removal of impurity' (Istihlak) through precise culinary transformation, ensuring the drink remains permissible despite fermentation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines a rigorous multi-stage boiling process to eliminate the 'khamar' (intoxicating) quality, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between mild, non-intoxicating beverages and those that cause intoxication. The inclusion of optional flavorings like saffron or ginger highlights the practical application of these legal boundaries in daily life.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, or from a man, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Fazzal, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa Al Sabaty who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws described the cooked (raisins) to me, how it is to be cooked until it comes to be Permissible, so heasws said to me: ‘Take a quarter of raisins and clean them, and pour twelve ratls (units of measurement) of water over it, then soak it overnight. So when it were the days of summer and you fear that it would simmer, keep it in an oven, a little full until it does not simmer. Then remove all of the water from it until when it is the morning, pour a measurement of water upon it sufficient to soak it. Then boil it until its sweetness is gone.

The remove the last water and pour the first water over it, then measure whole of it. So look at how much water there is, then measure a third of it and place it in the vessel which you intend to cook it, and pour a measurement of water which would submerge it, and measure it with a cane and make its measurement with a cane or a stick, so limit it upon the measure of when the water ends up to. Then boil the other third until the remaining water evaporates. Then boil it by the fire and do not cease to boil it until the two-thirds evaporates and there remains the third.

Then take for every quarter of a ratl of the honey, so boil it until its foam goes away and the mist of the honey goes away in the cooking. Then stir it with the stick with an intense stirring until it mixes up, and if you so desire to you can aromatise it with something from the saffron or with something from the ginger, so do it. Then drink it and if you would like its remaining to be prolonged with you, so keep it clean’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan or a man from Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabatiy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once explained for me how to cook raisins until the brew becomes lawful. He (the Imam) said, ‘Take one quarter of raisins and clean them. Pour twelve ritl of water on them, then soak for one night. If it is summer and you are afraid of its simmering, keep it in an oven, which is full a little so it does not simmer, then remove all the water from it. In the morning, pour water on it so that it is covered with water. Thereafter, boil it until its sweetness is gone.

Thereafter, remove the other water and pour on it the first water. Thereafter, measure all of it and see how much the water is. Thereafter, measure one-third of it and pour it in the pot in which you want to cook it. Pour enough water to cover it, then measure it with a stick and keep its size and measurement by a stick or reed and mark it at the surface of the water. Thereafter, boil the other third until the remaining water goes, then boil it on fire and keep boiling until two-thirds are gone and only one-third is left.

Thereafter, for every quarter take one ritl of honey and boil it until its scum and suds and blur of honey is gone from the cooking. Thereafter, beat it with a stick or such thing firmly until it is mixed and if you like, you can mix fragrance with saffron or ginger, you can do so, then you can drink it. If you like it to remain with you for a longer time then clean it properly.’”
